Sensory Tri-View, rung 2p: the audit's offenders, each with its picture

16 November 2026. Every picture is the True-Person view from the scene of record, the piece as it stands today. Seconds are the video player's, with the scene's second beside them.

A red bar marks what looks wrong. A green bar marks the same thing where it is right. A yellow ring is on the spot. Nothing in the engine has been changed for this list.

Making the pictures changed the count. Ten of the fourteen show in the piece and wait for your ruling, each with its picture. Two show nothing a still can hold. Two are not offenders after all.

To rule on: ten you can see

For each: what you see, why it happens, what a fix would change, and my pick.

  • O1With his eyes shut, the window sill breaks into white wedges.
    Eyes open at player 28.3 s (scene 22.6), against eyes shut at player 31.3 s (scene 25.0). He sits on the bed in both. The second is the first as he remembers it.
    What you see
    Eyes open: the sill is one clean ledge. Eyes shut: the top of the sill is broken into white wedges with black between them.
    Why
    His eyes see the top of the sill almost edge-on, so their picture has a single row of pixels for it. With his eyes open the engine does not use that row: it draws the face from the sill's known shape. For the last picture he held, it uses the row.
    If fixed
    The last picture he held is drawn by the same rule as the picture he sees, for every thing with a face seen edge-on.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O2The end of the east wall is a row of notches, and dots run beside a tree trunk.
    Player 82.0 s (scene 65.6), at the window.
    What you see
    The end of the room's east wall is a row of sharp notches. A row of dark dots runs beside the left tree's trunk. The right tree's crown has one clean outline.
    Why
    The wall's end and the trunk are each drawn twice at once: by the pixels of his eyes' picture, and by the thing's known shape. The two drawings do not lie on each other, and the gap between them shows. The crown is drawn once.
    If fixed
    One drawing for each such face, as the crown has.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O3With his eyes shut, the window's glass leaf loses its reflection.
    Eyes open at player 31.6 s (scene 25.3), against eyes shut at player 33.5 s (scene 26.8). The second is the first as he remembers it.
    What you see
    Eyes open: the open glass leaf carries a grey, grainy reflection. Eyes shut: the reflection is gone.
    Why
    The glass is the one thing in the room with no known shape and no place in the last picture he held. Its reflection is drawn only while his eyes are open.
    If fixed
    The reflection he last saw stays in the last picture, like everything else in it.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O5The remembered sun folds up and turns one flat grey.
    Player 105.3 s (scene 84.3), his eyes shut in the sun.
    What you see
    The remembered sun's disc is folded into an irregular shape with creases, in one flat pale grey. The remembered bushes beside it keep their round shape, and the remembered sky and ground carry soft light and dark bands.
    Why
    The sun is built apart from every other thing. It has its own ripple, which folds the disc, and its own memory look, with no bands of light.
    If fixed
    The remembered sun is drawn by the rule for every remembered thing that is small in his view: it keeps its disc, sways as a whole, and carries the bands.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O6In a blink, the remembered back of a thing stays lit while everything around it goes dark.
    A blink at player 90.1 s (scene 72.1), at the window. It lasts six frames. The same happens in every blink while he thinks of what he looks at.
    What you see
    With the lids shut, the half of each crown his eyes see goes dark, and so do the sky, the ridge and the ground. The pale half of each crown, its remembered back, stays as bright as before.
    Why
    The lids darken the picture he sees. By your ninth review they also darken the remembered ground and sky behind near things. They do not darken the remembered back of a thing.
    If fixed
    A remembered face inside his field of view goes dark with the lids, as the remembered sky behind a tree already does. What he remembers outside his field of view stays lit.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O7The back of a tree comes in pale, but the ground behind a bush comes in as if he saw it.
    Player 82.0 s (scene 65.6), before he thinks of the view, against player 88.0 s (scene 70.4), while he thinks of it.
    What you see
    Before the thought, every place his eyes cannot see is black. With the thought, the back of each crown fills in pale, plainly a memory. The ground behind each bush fills in looking exactly like the ground he is seeing.
    Why
    The back of a thing is drawn in memory's oldest look, by your word of 12 November that the unseen side of a thing and the memory of a thing are one. The ground, range and sky behind a near thing are drawn in memory's freshest look, which is close to the seen look.
    If fixed
    The ground and sky behind a near thing come in pale too. From this camera each bush and tree would then carry a pale patch behind it for as long as he thinks of the view.
    My pick
    Your call. I lean to fix, and would send a still of it before it goes into the piece.
  • O8As his eyes open after the sun, pale patches flash behind every bush and tree.
    From player 111.3 s (scene 89.0). The patches fade over about half a second.
    What you see
    Eyes shut: the remembered ground is one dim surface. As the lids part: a pale patch stands behind each bush and tree, brighter than anything around it. Eyes open: those places are black again.
    Why
    While his eyes are shut, the ground behind the bushes is part of the last picture he held, in memory's dim look. At the first frame of the opening that part alone changes over to a fresh picture at full brightness, while the rest of the last picture is still fading out. At the two earlier openings (player 31.3 and 33.8 s) the outside shows only through the window and nothing can be seen.
    If fixed
    The ground behind the bushes keeps the last picture's look and fades out with it.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O9A touch's spark starts at a joint, not at the place that is touched.
    The simulated mannequin sitting up in bed, enlarged. Player 24.8 s (scene 19.9): his left hand lands on his left thigh.
    What you see
    The hand's spark starts on the touch and runs up the arm. The thigh's spark, for the same touch, starts at the knee, a thigh's length from the touch, and runs past the touch to the hip.
    Why
    A spark starts at one fixed point per body part. For the hand that point is the hand. For the forearm it is the elbow and for the upper arm the shoulder, the end nearer his head. For the thigh it is the knee and for the shin the ankle, the end farther from his head.
    If fixed
    Every spark starts at the touched patch and runs from there up the limb to his head.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O11The pain in his right hand jumps between the whole hand and a small patch.
    The simulated mannequin at the window, from behind, enlarged four times. Player 84.1 s (scene 67.3) against player 99.4 s (scene 79.5).
    What you see
    With both hands on the sill, the hurt right hand looks like the unhurt left hand: one magenta patch each. With the hands off the sill, the right hand is red all over.
    Why
    His right hand hurts from the knock on the table at player 37 s to the end. While the timeline names a touch on that hand (the rub, the phone, the sill), the pain is drawn only on the touched patch, mixed into touch's magenta. While it names none, the pain lights the whole hand red. It changes over at player 38, 43, 46, 64, 81, 91 and 131 s.
    If fixed
    A pain that lasts stays on the whole hurt part until it fades. A touch on that part shows on its own patch as well. One more difference in the same rule has nothing to see in this piece, and I would settle it at the same time: a pain's brightness leaves out the strength the timeline gives it, which touch and pleasure use.
    My pick
    Fix.
  • O13The rings of a far sound start in mid-air, short of where the sound comes from.
    A bird's call at player 83.6 s (scene 66.9), against the phone's chime at player 111.2 s (scene 89.0).
    What you see
    The bird calls from the ridge. Its rings start at a point in the air over the bushes. The phone's rings start at the phone.
    Why
    A sound from farther than 6 m is drawn as starting 6 m from his head, on the line to its source. Every other far thing is placed at the distance he believes it to be.
    If fixed
    The rings start at the believed place of their source, here the ridge.
    My pick
    Fix. The rest of O13 in the outline is rules that name this stand-in room (one window, a far view called ridge, ground and sun, a reach of 6 m). They show nothing in this room and belong to the real room of rung 5.

Nothing a still can hold: two

  • O4With his eyes shut, the parts of his body he last saw sway more than the rest of his body.
    No picture: it shows only in motion, and it is small. In the doze (player 31 to 34 s, your clip 3) the pieces of his knees he last saw sway by about 3 cm. His arm beside them, drawn from his body's known shape, sways by about 1 cm.
    Why
    His own body has a small ripple, by your word that he feels his body at every moment. That holds for the parts drawn from his body's known shape. The parts of his body in the last picture he held take the full ripple, as remembered furniture does.
    If fixed
    One small ripple for all of his body, seen last or not.
    My pick
    Fix. It follows your own word, and it changes little.
  • O10Cold air shows only on the part of him the timeline names.
    No picture. The one cold-air event of the piece is on his face at the window, player 82 to 90 s. Its strength is 0.14 at its start and falls from there, and his face is turned away from the True-Person camera.
    Why
    Warmth appears by itself on every part of his skin the sun reaches. Cold air appears only on the parts the timeline lists, and it lists his face alone.
    If fixed
    Cold air would appear by itself on every bare part the window's air reaches. That needs a measure of how far the air carries into the room, which the stand-in room does not have.
    My pick
    Leave it for rung 4, where the timeline comes from your performance, and rung 5, the room.

Not offenders after all: two

Each turned out to be one rule once I had to show it.

  • O12Withdrawn. His awareness dims some glows and not others.
    No picture: the difference is a few percent of brightness.
    Why
    While he dozes he is 40 to 60 percent aware. The glows the engine works out by itself, such as his feet on the floor, dim to that. The ones the timeline names, such as the pain and the warmth on his face, keep the strength the timeline gives them. That is one rule: the timeline's own number already says how strongly he feels the thing at that moment.
    My pick
    No change.
  • O14Withdrawn. "Eyes open" is read at three positions of the lids.
    No picture: nothing differs.
    Why
    The three positions answer three different questions. Which picture to keep as the last one: lids nearly fully open. When the eyes count as shut: lids fully closed. Whether they still take in the far view: lids less than half closed.
    My pick
    No change.
